items_missed: No 'How are you today?' or any opening rapport question.

No agenda statement at the top of the call - never told her what the call would cover or that it would take 10-15 minutes, and never asked 'sound good?'. The pricing preview came mid-call after probing was already done.
Never asked whether she needs packing services - only asked for a box count.
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops.
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?').
All three headline differentiators skipped: No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000), Meet Your Mover, and On-Time Guarantee were never mentioned.
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch - said 'nothing additional' generally but never listed no credit card fees / no transportation fees / no fuel surcharge / no assembly fees.
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing - no 'prep shortens the move and lowers your bill', no consolidation examples, no take-a-carload tip.
Never said 'no deposit' in those words, and never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or 'reply with any corrections'.
Referred to 'business hours' without ever stating the actual hours.
Never used the customer's name once in a 15-minute call - and closed with 'Yes, sir' and 'Sir, bye-bye' to a female customer.
top_strength: Handled the day-of-week pricing question cleanly and honestly - explained that Tue/Wed/Thu are all the same discounted tier so she would not save by shifting days, rather than letting her believe a switch would save money. He also gave a well-reasoned, transparent estimate: named the 4-mover/2-truck 6.5-8.5 hour range, told her he was deliberately quoting on the safe side, and reassured her they only bill actual time used.
coaching_note: The three differentiators (No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) and the entire Save Your Ass prep speech were skipped - that's 30 of the 31 points he lost. Add those two blocks right after the pricing rate and this call jumps into the 80s. Also: get her name into the conversation and stop closing with 'sir' when you haven't confirmed it.
phone_presence_notes: Plenty of 'awesome/perfect/great news' affirmations but they repeat verbatim, he never used her name once, there was no rapport or humor, and he closed by calling a female customer 'sir'.
audio_review_reason: Two signals worth verifying on audio: the rep said 'I'm sorry, one more time' early on (possible line/audio quality issue), and he repeatedly addressed a female customer as 'sir' at close - need to confirm whether that is the rep or a transcription artifact before coaching on it.
